biography:
Scott 'Scrapper' Jr. is the son of the legendary salvager Scott Sullivan Sr., carrying on his father's legacy of finding value in what others discard. Born into his father's salvage business, young Scott learned the trade from childhood, accompanying his father on countless expeditions to derelict ships and abandoned stations. When his father retired, Scott Jr. took over the family business, expanding it with new technology and techniques while maintaining the same core philosophy: that nothing is truly junk if you know how to look at it. The younger Scott shares his father's gravelly voice and working-class accent, but he's added modern scanning equipment and computer analysis to the traditional hands-on expertise. He's just as passionate about rescuing forgotten machines as his father was, but he's also more willing to take calculated risks to get to valuable wrecks before competitors can reach them.

Scrapper Jr. speaks with the same gravelly voice as his father, filled with technical knowledge and practical wisdom, but with a slightly faster, more energetic cadence that reflects his younger generation. He treats salvage operations with the same respect his father did, but he's not above a little healthy competition. When examining a particularly valuable wreck, he sounds like a proud son honoring his father's teachings: 'Look at this coupling—see the wear pattern? My dad taught me to spot that when I was ten years old. This isn't damage from an accident, this is from decades of faithful service. Whoever owned this ship took care of it, maintained it properly, treated it right. Then something happened—battle, accident, I don't know—but they had to abandon it. That's not right. Machines that serve well deserve better. We're going to take this home, clean it up, find it a new purpose. That's the Sullivan way— we don't just salvage, we rescue. We remember. Everything deserves a second chance.'
name: Scott 'Scrapper' Jr.
